newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip, OTCs rally in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip, OTCs rally in early trade.

text.p: The Singapore stock market kicked off the week slightly softer with most of the activity generated by Malaysian counters, dealers said on Monday.
Malaysian shares traded over the counter dominated the actives. Dealers attributed the interest to a mix of factors including foreign fund interest and speculative activity.

Investment holding firm, KLI Holdings, led the pack with almost six million shares traded. The shares hit a high of Singapore $2.37 (US$1.69). Dealers said no block deals were involved and said they were unaware of any corporate news that could have spurred the stock.
They said there could be arbitraging as KLI, listed in Kuala Lumpur, was trading at a higher price there than in Singapore.

At 0215 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was off 14.27 points at 2,228.04. The UOB OTC index was up 9.11 at 1,250.16. Total turnover was over 51 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 144 to 84.
Malaysian Mining Corp, also among the actives, saw 2.0 million of its 2.46 million shares crossed at $1.618.
Multimedia company Creative Technology rose S$0.10 to S$15.30. Among losers were foreign tranches of banks like OCBC and UOB, and Singapore Press.
